home.eyebrow: Basic electricity, Department of Physics, Lund University
home.description: A collection of simple, presentation-ready electricity simulations for lectures and self-study. Practice building circuits, explore electrostatics, and visualize three-phase power, and continue until you have a strong intuition for how electric circuits and fields behave.

electrostatics.title: Electrostatics
electrostatics.description: Place and move around positive and negative point charges on the board to build an electrostatic scene.
electrostatics.instructions: Choose a charge polarity, then click on the board to place it. Clicking an existing charge adds +1 or -1 depending on the selected button, and dragging lets you move it.
electrostatics.boardHint: Click to place a charge, click again to add charge ±1, and drag to move.

electrostaticsMaterials.title: Electrostatics Materials
electrostaticsMaterials.description: A separate sandbox for conductors, dielectrics, and material-boundary electrostatics.
electrostaticsMaterials.instructions: Choose metal, dielectric, + charge, or - charge, then click on the board to place it. Drag pieces or charges to move them, and use the lower-right handle on a piece to resize it.
electrostaticsMaterials.solverNote: This sandbox now includes a first-pass material-aware field solver. Charges drive the field, dielectric regions change the response, metal regions are approximated as floating equipotential pieces, and the board renders both the potential landscape and field lines.
electrostaticsMaterials.boardHint: Click to place a square piece or point charge. Drag to move. Use the bottom-right handle on a piece to resize. Choose Remove object and click an object to delete it.

threePhase.title: Three-Phase Current
threePhase.description: Adjust Y and delta loads, then compare branch currents. Compare line currents, neutral current, phasors, and waveforms. Click the circuit diagram to expand it, and hover over a load to see its current.

circuitBuilder.title: Circuit Builder
circuitBuilder.description: Build a circuit and solve for potentials and currents. Suggestion: build a circuit and calculate currents and potentials by hand first. Then use the simulation to check your answers.
circuitBuilder.selectInfo: Drag to move nodes, voltmeters, and probes. Double-click a component to change its value. Double-click a wire or click a node to split it.
circuitBuilder.wireInfo: Click two points or nodes to draw a wire between them.
circuitBuilder.resistorInfo: Click the board to place a resistor. Double-click its body to edit the resistance.
circuitBuilder.idealBatteryInfo: Click the board to place an ideal voltage source. Double-click its plates or label to edit voltage.
circuitBuilder.realBatteryInfo: Click the board to place an ideal battery in series with a 1 Ω resistor. The resistor can be edited separately.
circuitBuilder.groundInfo: Click a node to make it the 0 V reference. Without ground, the first battery negative terminal is used.
circuitBuilder.currentProbeInfo: Click a wire or component to show the current through it.
circuitBuilder.potentialProbeInfo: Click a node to show its potential relative to ground. Move it with Select.
circuitBuilder.voltmeterInfo: Click two nodes to measure voltage between them, starting with the higher potential. Move it with Select.
circuitBuilder.ohmmeterInfo: Click two nodes to measure resistance. It only works when the circuit has no voltage source.
circuitBuilder.eraseInfo: Click probes first to remove them, or click a component to erase it.
circuitBuilder.instructions: Choose a component, then click the board. Wires and volt/ohm-meters use two clicks. Drag nodes and components to reshape the circuit. Double-click components to edit their values, double-click wires to split them, and click nodes to split them.
circuitBuilder.emptyState: Place a resistor, battery, wire, or ground to start.
circuitBuilder.noGround: Place a battery or set a ground node to solve the circuit.

phasorDiagram.title: Phasor Diagrams
phasorDiagram.description: Here you can explore the relationship between a rotating voltage phasor and the sinusoidal waveform it represents.
phasorDiagram.formulaHint: The phasor length corresponds to the amplitude. The instantaneous voltage is given by its vertical projection.
phasorDiagram.diagramLabel: Interactive phasor diagram linked to a sinusoidal voltage graph

rlcCircuit.title: RLC Circuit
rlcCircuit.description: Explore a series resistor, capacitor, and inductor driven by an AC voltage. Compare selectable voltages on an oscilloscope.
rlcCircuit.scopeLabel: Oscilloscope showing two selectable voltage channels in a series RLC circuit
rlcCircuit.phasorLabel: Phasor diagram showing resistor, capacitor, inductor, and source voltage
